     2	
     3	## A. The page opens on the served snapshot's day (built)
     4	
     5	**Defect** (`SERVING-WHILE-WRITING-RESULT.md`, finding 2): at start the page shows its embedded snapshot, then replaces it with the
     6	served library (`bootstrap.loadLibrary` → `library.setDataset`), whose clamp keeps the embedded day. A shell built on one day and opened
     7	on a later one therefore shows the shell's day, not the latest completed day. `thesis-ui.md`: "The supplied snapshot defines the
     8	displayed date."
     9	
    10	**Rule:** the library has no date control of its own (its day is set only when it is created and in `setDataset`, searched); the
    11	person changes dates in the explorer and the drawer, which keep their own state. So: the page's one automatic read
    12	(`bootstrap.loadLibrary`, run once at start) shows the served snapshot's `as_of`; every other replacement keeps today's verified clamp
    13	(`verify-library.mjs`, "library day clamps before replacement"); a failed read keeps the embedded snapshot silently, as
    14	`thesis-ui.md` specifies ("Automatic API loading keeps the current snapshot when unavailable"), a limitation recorded for Alex.
    15	
    16	**Owner:** `components/library.js` `setDataset(input, { day } = {})`: with a day, the library shows it, clamped to the new history;
    17	without, today's behaviour. `bootstrap.loadLibrary` passes `{ day: next.as_of }`. `thesis-ui.md` says it.
    18	
    19	**Proof ($0):** a test of `setDataset` with and without `{ day }`; the existing clamp check unchanged; the paused-writer test re-run
    20	with the page check asserting the displayed day and the question identities against the served response; the production shell against
    21	a new-system store shows the served `as_of`.
    22	
    23	## B. The first day of a live store (not built; an operating rule, recorded)
    24	
    25	**Finding 1:** before any day of a store completes, `service.default_as_of` falls back to the latest judgement's day, so the default
    26	views serve the day in progress. **Readers of that default** (searched): `bundle.library`, `bundle.thesis_bundles`, `idea.py`,
    27	`search.py`, `service.py` (views, a view, evidence, history, changes, the day's items, the evaluation route), and MCP's start
    28	(`scripts/hivemind_mcp.py`, the object list). Changing the default would change every one of them; a `None` default breaks several that
    29	compare dates. Census: 0 of 143 stored `views.sqlite` files hold processing steps, judgements and no completed day; the state lasts
    30	only from a new store's first write to the end of its first day.
    31	
    32	**Enforced on every read (version 3, council round 47: a start-time check admits a store that is empty at start and later reaches the
    33	state).** `service.first_day_unfinished(conn)` is true when a store has a processing step and no completed day. It is checked on each
    34	read, at the one place each entry point opens the ledger for a request: the API's `Connections.__enter__` (every GET route and
    35	`POST /ideas`) raises `service.NotReady`, answered **503** "the store's first day has not completed"; the MCP server wraps each tool
    36	with the same check and raises the same error. An explicit `as_of` does not bypass it: until the first day completes nothing is served.
    37	An empty store (no step) is read as today (no judgement: the library refuses for want of a completed day). A legacy ledger with no day
    38	records (no step) is read as today. A crash-left store in that state is refused for as long as it stays in it (until a day is
    39	completed or the store is replaced), not only "to the end of its first day". MCP's object list, computed at its start, stays as today
    40	(stale for objects that appear later: a recorded limitation, not this slice). Every reader of `default_as_of` keeps its default.
    41	
    42	**Tests through the real entry points:** one API process started on an empty temporary store: `/library` refused for want of a
    43	completed day; a processing step and a judgement written (the first day unfinished): `/days` and `/library` 503 with the message;
    44	the day completed: `/library` 200 as of that day. The MCP tools called with the module loaded on the same three states (503-equivalent
    45	error, then a library). `docs/poc/service.md` states the rule.
    46	
    47	## Status after round 48 (2026-11-16)
    48	
    49	- **A built and proved:** `verify-library.mjs` 11 of 11 in headless Chrome (`library-check.txt`); the paused-writer check re-run
    50	  (`serving-while-writing.txt`): a fresh page during 2026-09-25 shows exactly the five questions served as of 2026-09-24, and on
    51	  2027-01-31 after its closing exactly the seven served as of that day.
    52	- **B not built; recorded as an open defect.** A check on every read still races the writer unless the check and the read share one
    53	  database snapshot (council round 48); holding a read transaction across a request can delay the writer's commits (the 2026-10-28 lock
    54	  halt); MCP builds its object list and index at start; the streamed Idea response sends its headers before opening its connections.
    55	  The state arises only on a new store's first day (or a store left there by a crash); 0 of 143 stored stores are in it; no new-system
    56	  store is served live today (the service serves production's sealed ledger). Design input for the fix, when a live new-system service is
    57	  designed: the reader table above, one snapshot for check and read per request, MCP's start, the streamed response, and a test that
    58	  pauses a request between check and read while the writer commits.

item.text:
**A’s code and saved checks support the startup-date fix, but the agreed page proof does not yet assert the page’s date.** The harness compares question text, not the displayed or selected day. In particular, the January 30 and 31 libraries contain the same seven questions, so their identities alone cannot prove that the page selected January 31. Add the page’s selected day to the probe and compare it with the served `as_of`; retain the identity check. [serving_while_writing.py](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/page-contract/serving_while_writing.py:118), [saved result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/page-contract/serving-while-writing.txt)

**B is correctly recorded as an open defect in the status page**, with the snapshot race, MCP startup and streamed response named as design inputs. The design itself still has a preceding section headed “Enforced on every read” describing the rejected version; remove or clearly mark it as a rejected proposal so it cannot be mistaken for built behaviour. [CURRENT_STATE.md](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/CURRENT_STATE.md:154), [LIVE-READ-DESIGN.md](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/page-contract/LIVE-READ-DESIGN.md:32)

After the date assertion, the next useful production work is the **$0 live-service design**: decide how a new store becomes readable, how each reader obtains a consistent completed-day snapshot without blocking the writer unduly, and how the page identifies an unavailable or older snapshot. Its first test should deliberately interleave a read with the first-day write and fail if any partial day is presented as complete. The new-system Idea planner remains a separate integration item.

CONSENSUS: no, because the saved page proof does not check the selected date and the B design still presents the rejected guard as enforced.
